reason: The cited evidence supports that Mg-containing HEAs can be metastable (E1) and that intermetallics like Mg2Si can precipitate from solid solution (E4), but no cited passage directly links intermetallic precipitation to disrupted protective oxide scales or degraded corrosion/oxidation resistance; E2 even suggests intermetallics can promote passivation, contradicting the proposed mechanism.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight HEA can be processed into a metastable solid-solution state
Isothermal annealing at ~400 °C triggers diffusion-limited nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallics (e.g., Mg2Si) at grain boundaries
Intermetallic precipitation disrupts uniform protective oxide scale (TiO2/Al2O3) formation
Disrupted oxide scale formation degrades corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-quenched state
